description: An interactive stereo sampler. It records, plays a selection out of the sample at a speed you set, tracks 1V per octave, and can cut the sample into slices and play them in turn

params.text: Sets the playback speed, -2x to +2x, default 1x; a negative speed plays the selection backwards and shows in red on the display
How much of the voltage at the speed input reaches the playback speed
How much of the voltage at the modulation input shifts the frequency of the module's own LFO
Sets the frequency of the module's own LFO, which can be driven as high as 8kHz
How much of the module's own LFO is added to the playback speed, which is what gives the scratching effect
Starts recording, and stops it when tapped again; held with shift, what is recorded is added to the end of the sample instead of replacing it
A tap starts playback from the beginning of the selection
A tap stops playback, and the next one carries on from where it stopped
Sets where in the sample the selection starts, which is where playback begins
Sets where in the sample the selection ends
Stretches the wave display vertically, and changes nothing about the sound
Shifts the playback in octaves
Sets a fade at the start and the end of playback to keep clicks out, from 0 to 100ms; it also sets the crossfade between the start of the sample and its reversed end, up to 1 second
Switched on, the sample plays only while the start gate is high
Switched on, the selection repeats; switched off, playback ends at the end of the selection
Sets the module's own LFO to unipolar, so it only ever adds to the playback speed
Sets the module's own LFO to unipolar and negative, so it only ever takes away from the playback speed
Switches the grid on and off. With the grid on, the sample is divided into equal slices and the controls of the slice sequencer are left out of use
Switched on, a random slice of the grid is picked at the end of each cycle; with the sample cycling that gives an endless run of slices
A tap steps on to the next stored slice and loads it
A tap steps back to the previous stored slice and loads it
Balances the sound on sound mix: fully anticlockwise is the module's own signal, the centre an even mix of the two, fully clockwise the incoming signal alone
Sets the yummer effect, which spreads the grains of the sample further apart in time
Sets the level of the yummer effect
Switches on the preview of the sound on sound mix while the module is not recording
Switches sound on sound on, so the incoming signal is mixed with the sampled one
Switched on, a random stored slice is picked at the end of each cycle, which works while the grid is off

inputs.text: One side of the stereo signal to be recorded; with neither input patched the module records itself as it plays
A pulse starts recording, and the next one stops it
A voltage shifting the frequency of the module's own LFO
A pitch voltage at 1V per octave, which plays the selection chromatically
A pulse starts playback from the beginning of the selection, and with GATED switched on a gate holds it
A pulse stops playback, and the next one carries on from where it stopped
A voltage moving the start of the selection
A voltage moving the end of the selection
A pulse resets the phase of the module's own LFO
A clock here sets the frequency of the module's own LFO, in place of the FREQ knob
A voltage moving the depth of the module's own LFO
0-10V picks which slice of the grid is played
A pulse deletes the current stored slice
A pulse loads the current stored slice as the playing selection
A pulse stores the current selection as a new slice
A pulse replaces the current stored slice with the current selection
A pulse steps on to the next stored slice and loads it
A pulse steps back to the previous stored slice and loads it
A pulse picks a random stored slice
0-10V picks which of the stored slices is the current one
A voltage setting the sound on sound mix
A voltage moving the playback speed
A pulse activates the grid
A pulse picks a random slice of the grid

outputs.text: One side of the stereo output
A pulse each time playback reaches the end of the selection

notes: right-clicking the wave display gives the editing commands: cut, copy, paste, delete, zero, invert, normalise, amplify, trimming, and rendering the selection as the new sample
dragging the playhead with the alt key held moves it with granular playback, and dragging with shift held scratches it, the pitch following the speed of the drag
cue points in a WAV file are read in as slices, and saving as WAV writes the start of each slice back out as a cue point
nothing plays until the sample buffer holds something: load a wav or aiff file from the menu, or record into it
menu: REC to PLAY crossfade time — sets the crossfade between the recording buffer and the playing buffer, from 0 to 2 seconds
ABORT RECORDING — ends a recording and keeps the sample that was there before it
DELETE ALL Slices (option key down!) — deletes every stored slice, and is taken only with the option key held while it is chosen
Open WAV or AIFF File... — loads a wav or aiff file as the sample
STOP AND SAVE RECORDING IN A FILE — ends a recording and writes it out as a file
STOP AND APPEND RECORDING to SAMPLE — ends a recording and adds it to the end of the sample
DELETE Current Slice — deletes the slice that is current
LOAD Current Slice — loads the current stored slice as the playing selection
ADD Slice — stores the current selection as a new slice
UPDATE Current Slice — replaces the current stored slice with the current selection
